t: The northern Hebrew kingdom, formed when the tribes broke from Solomon’s heir c. 930 BCE, ruled from Samaria after Omri.
Larger and richer than Judah, it fielded 2,000 chariots against Assyria at Qarqar in 853 BCE under King Ahab.
Assyria took Samaria in 722 BCE and deported its people, giving rise to the legend of the Ten Lost Tribes.
dyk: Assyrian scribes went on calling Israel ‘the House of Omri’ for well over a century, long after Jehu had wiped out Omri’s dynasty.
ev: The northern tribes reject Rehoboam at Shechem and make Jeroboam I king
Omri founds the new capital of Samaria
Ahab fights Shalmaneser III of Assyria at the Battle of Qarqar
Jehu’s coup destroys the House of Omri; Jehu pays tribute to Assyria
Reign of Jeroboam II, Israel’s last period of prosperity
Tiglath-pileser III annexes Galilee and Gilead
Samaria falls to the Assyrians after a long siege
Sargon II deports some 27,000 people and creates the province of Samerina

f.capital: Shechem; later Tirzah; from c. 880 BCE Samaria
